questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Within Europe, good academic standing and a nice city to live in as a student.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Much better than I had ever hoped.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. There are student organisations such as the Erasmus Student Network and the school's International Office which offer assistance and help you get settled and start your semester without any stress.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance with my registration, transportation and finding student accommodation on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were apartments with private rooms and shared bathrooms and kitchens. There were also some apartments where you could share a room with another student. There were also few apartments that were studios for one person.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You had to cook for yourself.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Sign up on time. The day that housing registration opened for the SSH, the rooms were booked within 5 minutes. The Netherlands already has a housing crisis, so finding a place to live is essential because it is not easy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had amazing roommates who were fellow exchange students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's a step-by-step, so it was not that difficult to navigate through.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: UU has its own portal for exchange applications and it guides you through your application.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could call the school and ask questions but the portal itself was so easy to figure out, so you didn't need too much help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. I had to change classes a few times and the student office was so helpful. It was not any issue for me to change, as long as I did it in the first teaching week.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to do everything on time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did level 3 courses, meaning they were meant for third year BA students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UU was similar to UCPH as they also have a block structure, at least in science. The exams were slightly different but it was not too foreign.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: "Nanomaterials", "Making modern science: a history of Chemistry", "Organometallic Chemistry" and "Persuasive Technologies"

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed the "Making modern science: a history of Chemistry" course, as it was not my usual chemistry course. There was focus on the history of chemistry and not the theoretical, experimental and calculation aspects.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to pay for some medication when I was sick and my insurance here in Denmark did not cover it, which was a bit annoying.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The Netherlands is cheaper than Denmark in a lot of aspects, so it was nice to spend slightly less money on things I needed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined the ESN, which was a great way to make local friends in Utrecht.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN, BuddyGoDutch, School-led initiatives such as the Wellness week, the sports arena which offered several sports activities for students at a decent price.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is an app called UniLife, which shows all the different events happening in the city for students and it's a great way to get out there and try things. Additionally, make sure to join the events held by the student organisations as they are a great way to meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See another city! NL is so small and their trains are convenient to get around. If you travel in groups, you get a discount as well. I also highly recommend to just explore and get to know the city you will be living in for the next few months.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. I never really felt homesick but having nice roommates and forcing yourself to try new things really helped with this.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join events and if you live on campus, go for dancing and drinks at Cambrigdebar! I don't drink myself but their drink selection and pricing was student friendly and they had good sodas.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not many because the Netherlands reminds me a lot of Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature, canals, flowers, etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Housing
2. Join events
3. Explore the city

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The SSH is the housing portal for students coming to study in the Netherlands.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people, exploring a new city, learning to live on my own and trying new things.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living away from home (in the start) as I had never lived away from my parents.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
